caption: R2 100 on the generator this month, more than we spent on medical aid. Is load shedding costing you more than you've actually added up?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R34 500
p/m salary
Living in Mthatha
slides.body:
Male, 30
Married, no kids yet
Job: Municipal town planner
Net salary: R34 500 p/m

slides.title: Bond
slides.body: We bought two years ago. The bond hasn't moved as much as everything around it has.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Big monthly shop, plus the load shedding stockpile of non-perishables
slides.body: We buy more tinned food than we used to. It's cheaper than losing a freezer full of meat.

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.body: Bought before the fuel price moved twice. I'd think harder about it now.

slides.title: Generator fuel & maintenance
slides.includes: Petrol for the generator, a service after eight months of daily use
slides.body: I didn't budget for this at all a year ago. Now it's just a line item.

slides.title: Takeaways during outages
slides.includes: The nights the stove's off for six hours and we give up on cooking
slides.body: We told each other it was maybe R500. It's R1 200. Load shedding makes you buy things.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Medical aid, petrol, phone & fibre, funeral policy, stokvel, insurance, savings
slides.body: Thirteen thousand six hundred rand of things that run whether or not the power does.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R34 500. On paper this is a comfortable salary. The generator line makes it feel less comfortable than it used to.

slides.title: I stopped guessing what load shedding was actually costing us
slides.body:
I uploaded three months of statements to Beyond Horizon and watched the generator fuel line grow month on month.

R2 100 this month, more than we spend on medical aid.

No bank login needed.
